I believe clear() will do what you want. It will delete the elements
of a vector and update the size to zero, but the underlying memory
will be unaffected. I'm not sure about the behaviour of resize(0).

Let me summarize how I understand the process should work. Either

1) A contributor does not have push access to our repo.

In this case the contributor forks our repo into their own github account, which gives them a local copy of the repo that tracks any changes we make. Effectively this is just like them cloning our repo but with the ability to save their commits on their github account.

Once the contributor is happy with their changes they make a pull request, denoting the local branch they want to merge from and the remote branch they want to merge into. When the merge is done github handles all the logistics of moving branches around.

Once Dan removed my permissions, this is the situation I was in only I wasn't prepared with a proper fork. It wasn't too hard to fork and then copy over my local changes to the fork.

2) a contributor has access to our repo.

In this case the contributor makes a branch, pushes changes to that branch, and makes a pull request denoting the source (now a branch within the repo instead of in a fork) and the destination (probably master).

Unfortunately there's no way we can allow people to handle merge requests without also allowing them to push to master directly - we just have to be courtious.

Also, it's probably good habit to start mentioning people who might be best suited for handling a particular pull request, especially if we have lots of potential mergers. Github allows @ mentions for this purpose.
